article_title: Student Behavior and Epistemological Framing: Examples from Collaborative Active-Learning Activities in Physics
citation: Rachel E. Scherr and David Hammer. (2007). Student Behavior and Epistemological Framing: Examples from Collaborative Active-Learning Activities in Physics. Submitted to Cognition and Instruction. https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Student+Behavior+and+Epistemological+Framing
title: Physics tutorials: worksheet-based group-learning activities replacing traditional recitation
description: Tutorials are worksheets that guide collaborative active learning in small groups around core conceptual issues identified by research as essential. In the studied course, the traditional TA-led recitation was replaced with tutorials in which students worked in small groups making predictions and comparing lines of reasoning, with TAs serving as facilitators rather than lecturers. The tutorials were constructed to emphasize reconciliation of everyday intuitive thinking with formal scientific thinking and to encourage explicit epistemological discussion.
requirements: Teaching assistants serve as facilitators rather than lecturers, engaging students in discussions of difficult concepts
constraints: The article reports the evidence for conceptual gains is almost exclusively pre- and post-testing, with little direct investigation of what happens during the activities
target_learners: junior and senior health and life science majors in large algebra-based introductory physics lectures of approximately 160 students
target_learning_goals: conceptual understanding of basic physics concepts and epistemological and metacognitive gains
examples: The Newton's third law truck-and-car tutorial, the free-body diagrams tutorial, and the electrostatics tutorial analyzed in this study
key_sources: Rachel E. Scherr and David Hammer. (2007). Student Behavior and Epistemological Framing: Examples from Collaborative Active-Learning Activities in Physics. Submitted to Cognition and Instruction. https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Student+Behavior+and+Epistemological+Framing

article_title: Tutor assessment of PBL process: does tutor variability affect objectivity and reliability?
citation: Sa Bidyadhar, Ezenwaka Chidum, Singh Keerti, Vuma Sehlule, Majumder Md. Anwarul Azim. (2019). Tutor assessment of PBL process: does tutor variability affect objectivity and reliability? BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-019-1508-z
title: University of the West Indies PBL tutorial assessment rating scale
description: A tutor rating instrument used to assess students' involvement and contribution in the PBL process under the Maastricht seven-step approach. It consists of 13 items covering 12 performance criteria (e.g., ability to clarify and analyze problems, generate learning objectives, critical thinking, team skills) plus one global assessment, rated on a six-point scale from Very Poor (0) to Excellent (5), with a maximum total score of 65. The article reports it has been used for more than 25 years and that an in-house evaluation in 2009 found 73% of facilitators found it acceptable and user-friendly.
requirements: Tutors familiar with the PBL process and trained in its assessment rubrics
constraints: The article notes process-oriented PBL instruments generally possess psychometric shortcomings limiting their use in high-stakes examinations
target_learners: third-year MBBS students in PBL tutorials
target_learning_goals: PBL process skills such as problem analysis, hypothesis generation, self-directed learning, and teamwork
examples: Used by tutors to rate each of the 14 PBL groups three times in this study, with PBL contributing only 5% weightage to summative assessment
key_sources: Sa Bidyadhar, Ezenwaka Chidum, Singh Keerti, Vuma Sehlule, Majumder Md. Anwarul Azim. (2019). Tutor assessment of PBL process: does tutor variability affect objectivity and reliability? BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-019-1508-z
